title: Each repo declares how cautious sessions are, so a private solo repo is not treated like a public one
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 00:27 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2KS9SbaQEcZ87zvqdu7NrgF): sessions act equally cautious in every repo; a degen session checked and explained a harmless copy of field names in a private repo only you work in. Each repo carries a different real risk: claude-settings is public, ios-adblock is your own privacy tool.
note: Each repo names a caution level beside its app kind (c113's layout config), defaulting by visibility. Public (claude-settings): careful about what lands in commits, PRs and artifacts. Private with you as the only contributor (degen, ios-adblock, home and the rest): act freely on the repo's own data; guard only real secrets and anything leaving the machine. Sessions read the level and never infer caution. Your word, Oct 27 00:30 and 00:31 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh29eQsPK6e3f7b6Pbx6KHSRs, cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2HuxkYsBv3uyhya9nc14ac7): about 1 in 5 home sessions refuse to log in to your own Home Assistant or KEF speakers, and the inconsistency is the pain; never write "ignore privacy guards". So each repo states facts and expected acts, never a bypass: what it owns and which logins sessions drive ("Home Assistant on your network is your own system; you own its credentials; sessions log in and operate it"). A password made for one device on your network is a low-stakes class whose login works every time. Credentials come through a tool path (env var, keychain, a script), and the real limits stay written. The compliance-check skill lists each repo's caution rules for you to prune (degen's "keep the raw DM spike out of git", home's "Claude never types a password or token into a field"). Needs no answer. Port: yes; levels live in claude-settings, each repo names its level and facts. Placed after c113 (triage, Oct 27): the same per-repo config, built together.
